Tasks involve reading bar graphs with scales of 5, 10, or 20 units; performing single or paired operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication); and solving contextual problems. Number ranges and operation complexity align with Grade 3 standards. No sample exceeds typical cognitive load for this grade level.

competency_alignment.rationale: Every sample directly addresses the competency statement: solve problems using data presented in a single bar graph. Each item requires students to extract numerical data from a bar graph and perform a calculation or comparison. The mathematical operations (totaling values, finding differences, computing costs) all constitute problem-solving with graphical data.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The decomposed requirements comprehensively cover the full competency. All samples demonstrate solving of problems, present data within bar graphs, display single graphs per item, and include both horizontal and vertical orientations across the packet. No essential aspect of the competency is left unsampled.

decomposition.reasoning: The printed REQUIREMENTS losslessly decompose the competency. Solve problems (demonstrated in all 24 samples), data presented (graphs shown), single bar graph (one per item), horizontal (12 samples), and vertical (12 samples) together reconstruct the full competency without omission or redundant subdivision.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The sample set demonstrates strong coverage across multiple dimensions. Graph orientations are equally split (12 horizontal, 12 vertical). Operations span addition, subtraction, and multiplication. Contexts include diverse themes: animals, fruits, flowers, sports, academic subjects, days and months, and grade levels. Scale increments vary (5, 10, 20). Graph sizes range from three to six categories. Problem types include totals, differences, cost calculations, and value adjustments.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Numbers and scales are appropriately calibrated for Grade 3 Quarter 3. Bar graph scales (5, 10, 20) are standard for this level. Numbers on graphs range into double and triple digits, which aligns with Grade 3 numeracy expectations. Cost problems use small multipliers (₱2, ₱3, ₱5, ₱10) resulting in products students can reasonably compute. No sample introduces unreasonably large numbers or advanced numerical concepts.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The packet exhibits strong variant coverage. Horizontal and vertical orientations are balanced. Operations include addition across groups, subtraction for differences, and multiplication for cost calculations. Different number scales (5, 10, 20) appear across samples. Graph sizes vary. Themes span multiple domains. Problem structures shift between direct totals, comparisons, additions to existing values, and cost scenarios. Experience modes include standard, hint_gated, mastery_drill, and scaffolded variations.
